column1: To make our economy stronger and more productive, we must make health care more affordable, and give families greater access to good coverage, and more control over their health decisions. I ask Congress to move forward on a comprehensive health care agenda–with tax credits to help low-income workers buy insurance, a community health center in every poor county, improved information technology to prevent medical errors and needless costs and association health plans for small businesses and their employees, and expanded health savings accounts.

Americans can expect some things of me, as well. My most solemn responsibility is to protect the American people. To do that job, I’ve made the defense of our country the first priority of my Administration. I will continue to deploy the resources and the resolve necessary to confront our enemies, and I will never waver in defending our nation against those who seek to do us harm.

When credible intelligence warrants, appropriate law enforcement and local officials are alerted. These warnings are, of course, meant to be secret. The fewer people who have access to them, the more effective they will be. We will continue to monitor threats and be prepared for any circumstances. I pledge to you that safety and security will remain the top priorities of my administration, as it has always been.

But the stakes for America are never small. If our country does not lead the the world into a more hopeful future, then who will? Our strategy begins with an unwavering commitment to winning the war on terror. We are confronting these enemies in Afghanistan, Iraq, and around the world. We're working with allies to stop terrorist acts, starve terrorist groups of funding, and deny them safe havens.

In all three aspects of our strategy -- security, democracy, and reconstruction -- we have made historic progress. We've defeated a brutal enemy. We're helping the people of Iraq to build a free society. And we're working with our allies to secure the peace. We've learned so much about the difficult nature of this struggle. My pledge to all-- the Iraqi people and the world-- is that we will not falter in the face of the enemy, and we will prevail.
